- [RCTS.1.2.31] **`runtime_fact_count`'s and `temporal_sequence`'s fields** —
  a fixture of either kind pins how many facts working memory holds after
  its inputs. A harness must load the compiled artefact into a fresh engine
  on the harness's mock clocks and give it the inputs below, in order,
  through the runtime's own interface. The runtime passes only when working
  memory then holds `fact_count_after` live facts.

  - `fact_count_after` (required), a non-negative integer.
  - `runtime_fact_count`'s inputs, each optional, in this order: `cache_seeds`,
    as [RCTS.1.2.25] has it; `asserts`, an array of objects, each a host
    assert carrying `schema`, a string, and optionally `slots`, an object, as
    an `assert` step carries them ([RCTS.1.2.28]); `generate_asserts`, an
    array of objects of `schema` and `slot_name`, strings, `count`, a
    non-negative integer, and optionally `start`, an integer, 0 when absent,
    each standing for `count` host asserts of `schema`, whose slot
    `slot_name` holds `start`, `start` + 1, and so on, in that order; and one
    pump, when `pump`, a boolean, is `true`. A fixture with none of them has
    the load as its only input.
  - `temporal_sequence`'s inputs: `steps`, the session's inputs as
    [RCTS.1.2.28] has them.
  - `tamper` (optional, `runtime_fact_count` only), an edit a harness must
    make to the compiled artefact before the load, as [RCTS.1.2.21] has it
    for this kind.
  - `add_compiled_code` (optional, `runtime_fact_count` only), an object of
    exactly one member, `node`, an integer N of at least 1. Before the load,
    and after `tamper`'s edit, a harness must append to the compiled
    artefact, after its last atom, one
    `CompiledCode` atom for each of the `arch` values `amd64`, `arm64`,
    `rv64g` and `rv64gc`, in that order, each with `node_id` N, `kind`
    `CODE_KIND_RHS` and a `body` of 64 octets of 0, its fields in ascending
    order ([RFCS.19.5]), and then recompute `dsc_sha256` as [RDSC.3.6]
    states. No compiler of this edition writes the atom ([RDSC.4c.3]), so
    this is how a fixture gives a runtime one for the architecture it runs
    on. A harness must fail a fixture whose artefact holds no `TerminalNode`
    whose `node_id` is N, or more than one.

  A harness must fail a fixture of either kind with no `fact_count_after`,
  and one whose value for any of these fields is not of the type stated here.
  It must fail a fixture of any other `expect.kind` that carries
  `add_compiled_code`.
